filth
filth

Aeschylus in The Theori (fr. 76): "Read πλέω γράσου τε καὶ ψόθου · οἷον, καὶ ῥύπου [full of stench and filth; that is, also of dirt]. Aeschylus in The Theori. And understand as if immediately after ψό [the syllable 'pso'] came Αἰσχύλος [Aeschylus]." DOBRAEUS in the index p. 735. Theognostus in Cramer's Anecd. Oxon. vol. 2 p. 53, 28, where he deals with nouns in -otos, says: ψοθοιὸς ὁ ἀκάθαρτος [psothoios, the unclean one].

Ψό [the syllable 'pso']: used of what is rotten and not pleasing; it is a clipped expression (Bernhardy: a clipping of an Attic expression; Dobraeus: a clipped expression). For they call it ψόθον [filth]. Aristophanes (fr. 706): “πλέω γράσου καὶ ψοθοίου καὶ ῥύπου γε καὶ ψόθου” [full of stench and filth and dirt and filth].
